The deadlift is the one exercise in Phase 3 where advanced intensity techniques are deliberately not applied. The deadlift is a high-skill, high-risk movement and the combination of near-maximal loads with techniques like cluster sets or forced eccentrics creates unnecessary injury risk. Instead, push the load as heavy as possible within perfect technique.
5 sets × 4 reps @ RPE 9. This is the heaviest the client will lift in the entire programme. Rest 3 minutes between sets. The final set should feel like there is one rep remaining — not zero. Never take the deadlift to absolute failure.

**Romanian Deadlift — Forced Eccentric with Intraset Stretch**
4 sets × 8 reps with a 5-second eccentric and a 3-second pause at the bottom in the fully stretched hamstring position. This combination — slow eccentric plus stretch pause — is one of the most potent hamstring hypertrophy techniques available and is supported by recent research on stretch-mediated hypertrophy. The load will need to be reduced significantly compared to normal RDL working weight — approximately 20–25% lighter. Rest 2 minutes.

**Hip Thrust — Mechanical Drop Set**
3 sets. Perform 10 reps of a standard barbell hip thrust to near failure. Without resting, remove the barbell and perform bodyweight hip thrusts to failure, focusing on a maximum glute squeeze at the top of every rep. Without resting, perform a 30-second isometric hold at the top position — hips fully extended, glutes maximally contracted. Rest 2 minutes. The glute is taken through three different stimuli in rapid succession.

**Lying Leg Curl — Myo-Reps with Forced Eccentric**
1 activation set of 12 reps with a 4-second eccentric. Then myo-rep clusters of 3 reps (maintaining the 4-second eccentric) with 5-breath rest periods. As with the leg extension on Tuesday, the combination of myo-reps and forced eccentrics on a leg curl creates an exceptional hamstring stimulus. Rest 90 seconds.

**Single-Leg Press — Rest-Pause**
3 sets each leg to technical failure, followed by 15-second rest and additional reps. Performing this unilaterally ensures no dominant leg compensation and forces each leg to work independently to true failure. Rest 60 seconds between legs.

**Seated Calf Raise — 1.5 Rep Method**
4 sets × 12 reps using the 1.5 rep method. Lower to full stretch, rise halfway, lower back to full stretch, rise to full contraction — one rep. The seated calf raise targets the soleus more than the standing version, and the 1.5 rep method ensures the soleus spends significant time under load in the stretched position. Rest 45 seconds.

### Week 10

The exercise selection remains identical to Week 9. The following progressions are applied.

**Load:** Increase all compound lift loads by the smallest available increment — 1.25 kg on upper body, 2.5 kg on lower body — where the Week 9 cluster sets or straight sets were completed at RPE 8–9 with good form. Do not increase load if form was compromised.

**Cluster set rest:** Reduce intraset rest from 20 seconds to 15 seconds on all cluster sets. This makes the second mini-set harder without changing the load, effectively increasing the intensity of the technique.

**Myo-rep activation sets:** Increase the activation set from 15 reps to 20 reps before beginning the myo-rep clusters. This deeper pre-fatigue means the clusters begin from a higher state of motor unit recruitment.

**Eccentric tempo:** Increase all forced eccentric tempos by one second — exercises previously performed with a 4-second eccentric now use a 5-second eccentric, and 5-second eccentrics become 6 seconds. This is a small change that creates a significant increase in time under tension.

**Final set intensity:** On one compound lift per session, take the absolute final set to **technical failure** — the point at which the next rep would involve form breakdown. This should happen on only one exercise per session and only on the final set. Do not take the deadlift to technical failure under any circumstances.

---

### Week 11

Week 11 is the peak intensity week of the entire programme — the hardest the client will train across the full twelve weeks. Recovery in the days surrounding this week is paramount.

**Monday and Thursday (Upper Body sessions):** Add one additional working set to every compound movement. The bench press, overhead press, pull-up, and row each gain one extra set compared to Week 10. This is a significant volume increase on top of the already elevated intensity — it will be demanding.

**Tuesday and Friday (Lower Body sessions):** Add one additional set to the squat, deadlift, and hip thrust only. Do not add sets to isolation exercises — the lower body is already under enormous stress from the compound work.

**Intensity techniques:** All techniques from Weeks 9 and 10 are maintained. On the myo-rep exercises, continue until only 2 reps can be completed rather than stopping at 3 — this pushes one step closer to absolute failure.

**New addition — Superset pairing on isolation work:** Pair antagonist muscle group isolation exercises into supersets to increase density and metabolic stress without adding time to the session. Suggested pairings:
- Tricep pushdown immediately followed by bicep curl (rest 60 seconds after the pair)
- Lateral raise immediately followed by face pull (rest 60 seconds after the pair)
- Leg extension immediately followed by leg curl (rest 90 seconds after the pair)

**Recovery flag for Week 11:** If the client reports two or more of the following — persistent soreness that has not resolved since the previous session, declining performance compared to Week 10, disrupted sleep, low mood, or elevated resting heart rate — reduce volume back to Week 9 levels for the remainder of the week and move into the Week 12 deload immediately. Pushing through genuine overreaching symptoms is counterproductive and potentially harmful. The goal of Week 11 is maximum productive stimulus, not maximum possible suffering.

---

### Week 12 — Deload

The deload is unchanged from the original programme. All intensity techniques are suspended. Return to straight sets of 3 × 8 at 60–65% of Week 11 loads. RPE should not exceed 6. The purpose of the deload is to allow the adaptations driven by Weeks 9–11 to consolidate — muscle growth continues to occur during the deload as inflammation resolves and protein synthesis catches up with the training stimulus. Many clients will look noticeably better at the end of Week 12 than they did at the end of Week 11 for exactly this reason.

# Full Integrated 12-Week Vegan Muscle Gain Programme
### Complete Summary Document

---

## Client Profile

**Age:** 26 | **Goal:** Hypertrophy | **Diet:** Strict vegan | **Experience:** Recreational lifter | **Equipment:** Full gym | **Daily protein target:** 150 g from plants only

---

## Programme Architecture at a Glance

| Phase | Weeks | Training Focus | Cardio Focus | Intensity Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 — Foundation | 1–4 | Movement quality, baseline volume | LISS only | RPE 6–7 |
| Phase 2 — Volume Accumulation | 5–8 | Volume increase, new techniques | LISS + MISS + HIIT | RPE 7–8 |
| Phase 3 — Intensification | 9–12 | Peak intensity, advanced techniques | LISS + HIIT maintained | RPE 8–9+ |

---

## Nutrition Framework

### Daily Targets

| Macro | Daily Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 150 g | Plant sources only, spread across 4–5 meals |
| Carbohydrates | 280–320 g | Adjust based on training days vs rest days |
| Fat | 60–75 g | Prioritise unsaturated sources |
| Calories | 2,300–2,550 kcal | Modest surplus of 200–350 kcal above maintenance |

Reassess caloric intake every two weeks. If weight is not increasing after two consecutive weeks, add 150–200 kcal per day. If weight is increasing faster than 0.5 kg per week, reduce by 100–150 kcal.

---

### Top Protein Sources

| Food | Protein per Serving |
|---|---|
| Seitan | 25 g per 100 g |
| Tempeh | 19 g per 100 g |
| Firm tofu | 17 g per 100 g |
| Edamame | 11 g per 100 g |
| Pea protein powder | 20–25 g per scoop |
| Brown rice protein powder | 20–22 g per scoop |
| Lentils (cooked) | 9 g per 100 g |
| Black beans / chickpeas | 8–9 g per 100 g |
| Hemp seeds | 10 g per 30 g |
| Nutritional yeast | 8 g per 2 tbsp |
| Soy milk | 6–8 g per 250 ml |
| Quinoa (cooked) | 4 g per 100 g |

---

### Daily Meal Structure (≈150 g protein)

**Meal 1 — Breakfast (≈35–40 g protein)**
Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu) with nutritional yeast, edamame, oats, and hemp seeds. Alternatively, soy milk protein porridge with pea protein powder, hemp seeds, and banana.

**Meal 2 — Pre-training snack (≈25 g protein)**
One scoop pea-rice protein blend shaken with oat or soy milk and a banana. Fast-digesting, easy on the stomach before training.

**Meal 3 — Post-workout meal (≈40 g protein)**
The most important meal of the day. Consume within 60–90 minutes of finishing training. See post-workout meal options below. Target 35–45 g protein and 60–90 g carbohydrates in this meal.

**Meal 4 — Afternoon or evening (≈30 g protein)**
Large lentil and black bean bowl with roasted vegetables and tahini dressing, or red lentil dal with basmati rice.

**Meal 5 — Evening snack (≈20 g protein)**
One scoop brown rice or pea protein stirred into oat porridge with nut butter, or a small smoothie with hemp seeds and soy milk.

---

### Post-Workout Meal Options

All meals deliver 36–48 g protein and 68–88 g carbohydrates. Rotate across the week for amino acid variety and dietary enjoyment.

| Meal | Key Ingredients | Protein | Carbs | Calories | Prep Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tempeh and Sweet Potato Bowl | 200 g tempeh, 250 g sweet potato, edamame, spinach, nutritional yeast | 42 g | 72 g | 580 kcal | 10 min |
| Pea Protein Smoothie Bowl | 2 scoops pea protein, oats, banana, hemp seeds, soy milk, frozen mango | 48 g | 78 g | 620 kcal | 5 min |
| Tofu Fried Rice | 250 g firm tofu, white rice, peas, corn, soy sauce, nutritional yeast | 38 g | 68 g | 540 kcal | 8 min |
| Seitan and White Bean Wrap | 150 g seitan, white beans, flour tortillas, salsa, rocket | 45 g | 74 g | 630 kcal | 5 min |
| Red Lentil Dal and Rice | Red lentils, basmati rice, coconut milk, tomatoes, spices, spinach | 36 g | 88 g | 580 kcal | 10 min |
| Edamame and Quinoa Salad | Quinoa, edamame, chickpeas, vegetables, tahini dressing, pumpkin seeds | 40 g | 70 g | 600 kcal | 0 min |
| Soy Milk Protein Porridge | Oats, soy milk, pea protein, hemp seeds, banana, almond butter | 38 g | 80 g | 610 kcal | 5 min |

---

### Protein Powder Recommendation

**First choice:** Pea and brown rice protein blend (70:30 ratio) from a third-party certified brand.

**Specific recommendations by tier:**

| Tier | Product | Protein per Serving | Certification | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Premium | Vivo Life Perform | 25 g | Informed Sport | Organic, full amino acid profile published, ~2.4 g leucine |
| Premium | Form Nutrition Perform | 30 g | Informed Sport | Pea, rice, and sacha inchi blend, naturally sweetened |
| Mid-range | Myprotein Vegan Blend | 22 g | Informed Sport | Best value, wide flavour range, widely available |
| Mid-range | Orgain Organic Sport | 30 g | USDA Organic | Strong US availability, chia seed addition |
| Alternative | Soy protein isolate | 22–25 g | Varies by brand | Complete amino acid profile, excellent leucine content |

Use one to two scoops per day to fill gaps. Whole food protein sources always take priority. Rotate between a pea-rice blend and soy isolate across the week for broadest amino acid coverage.

---

### Supplement Stack

| Supplement | Dose | Timing | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Creatine monohydrate | 3–5 g daily | Any time, consistent daily use | Especially impactful for vegans with lower baseline muscle creatine stores |
| Vitamin B12 | 250 mcg daily or 1,000 mcg every other day | Morning with food | Not found in plant foods — essential |
| Vitamin D3 (vegan/lichen) | 1,000–2,000 IU daily | Morning with food | Particularly important in winter months |
| Algae-based omega-3 | 250–500 mg EPA/DHA daily | With a meal | Supports inflammation management and recovery |
| Iodine | 150 mcg daily | With food | Unless using iodised salt consistently |

---

### Flex Meal Day

**Day:** Saturday throughout all 12 weeks
**Structure:**

- **Morning:** Normal programme breakfast — do not begin the flex day at breakfast
- **Midday:** Relaxed vegan meal, no tracking required
- **Evening:** Main flex meal — freely chosen, fully vegan, eaten mindfully
- **Non-negotiable:** Remains fully vegan at all times
- **Alcohol:** Optional, keep to one or two drinks maximum, stay well hydrated
- **Sunday:** Return to normal programme eating immediately, no compensation or restriction

**Flex meal ideas at home:** Loaded vegan nachos, vegan mac and cheese, vegan burgers with fries, curry feast, pasta carbonara or bolognese, vegan cheeseboard and sharing platter.

**Flex meal ideas eating out:** Dedicated vegan restaurants, Indian, Japanese, Middle Eastern, Mexican, Italian with vegan modifications.

**Physical expectations after flex day:** Temporary weight increase of 0.5–1.5 kg from glycogen and water — not fat. Resolves within 48–72 hours. Do not weigh in on Sunday morning. Expect potentially improved gym performance on Monday or Tuesday from glycogen supercompensation.

**Caloric compensation:** On flex meal days, do not restrict the following day. Return to normal eating on Sunday. The flex day sits within a weekly caloric average that still supports muscle gain.

---

## Training Programme

### Weekly Schedule

| Day | Resistance Session | Cardio |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | Upper Body A — Push Focus | 15 min LISS post-session |
| Tuesday | Lower Body A — Quad Focus | No cardio |
| Wednesday | Active recovery and mobility | 25–35 min LISS (primary cardio day) |
| Thursday | Upper Body B — Pull Focus | 15 min LISS post-session |
| Friday | Lower Body B — Posterior Chain | No cardio |
| Saturday | Flex meal day | LISS (Phase 1) / HIIT (Phase 2–3) / Full rest |
| Sunday | Full rest | No cardio |

---

### Cardio Overview by Phase

**Heart rate zones for a 26-year-old (HRmax ≈ 194 bpm):**
- LISS: 116–136 bpm (60–70% HRmax) — conversational pace
- MISS: 136–155 bpm (70–80% HRmax) — elevated but sustainable
- HIIT work intervals: 165–184 bpm (85–95% HRmax) — maximum sustainable effort

**HIIT protocol (Saturday, Phase 2 and 3):**
5-minute warm-up, then 20 seconds maximum effort / 40 seconds easy recovery. 10 rounds in Week 5, building to 12 rounds by Week 7 and maintained through Phase 3. Preferred equipment: stationary bike. 5-minute cool-down plus stretching.

**Cardio calorie compensation:** Add approximately half to two-thirds of estimated cardio calories back into daily food intake on training days. Practically: an extra half cup of oats or a medium sweet potato plus a small protein source on cardio days.

**Signs cardio volume is too high:** Persistent unresolved muscle soreness, declining gym performance, poor sleep, elevated resting heart rate, low mood or motivation. If two or more signs appear simultaneously, remove one cardio session for one week before reassessing.

## Phase 3 — Intensification (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Maximum hypertrophic stimulus through advanced intensity techniques applied to a slightly reduced volume base.
**Intensity:** RPE 8–9+ | **Rest periods:** 2–3 minutes compound, 60–90 seconds isolation

### Intensity Techniques — Summary Definitions

**Cluster sets:** Break a set into two mini-sets separated by 15–20 seconds intraset rest. Allows heavier loading than continuous sets. Used on compound lifts.

**Myo-reps:** Activation set of 15–20 reps to near failure, followed by clusters of 3–5 reps with 5-breath rest periods until minimum rep count cannot be maintained. Accumulates high volume of effective reps near failure. Best on isolation and machine exercises.

**Mechanical drop sets:** Change exercise or body position rather than load when approaching failure, moving to a mechanically advantageous position to continue the set. Keeps load constant while extending the set.

**Forced eccentrics:** Slow the lowering phase to 4–6 seconds to increase time under tension and muscle damage. Load reduced by 15–25% to accommodate tempo.

**1.5 rep method:** Full rep, halfway return, back to start, full rep — counts as one repetition. Doubles time in the stretched position and increases eccentric load.

**Intraset stretching:** Deliberate 2–3 second pause in the fully stretched position on every rep. Exploits stretch-mediated hypertrophy — a particularly potent stimulus for muscle growth.

**Rest-pause sets:** Take a set to technical failure, rest 15–20 seconds, perform additional reps. Repeat once more if possible. Extends effective volume beyond normal failure point.
